result.text:
HALVARD SYSTEMS - ACCOUNTING POLICY MANUAL (excerpt), effective 2026-01-01
Applies to Halvard Systems Inc. (US), Halvard Systems Ltd (UK), Halvard Systems GmbH (DE).

1. Posting authority. Senior accountants may post manual journal entries up to USD 10,000
   per entry (local-currency entries are measured at the month-end rate of the entry month).
   Any entry above USD 10,000 must be routed to the Controller with an approval request
   (request_approval) immediately after posting; it remains pending until approved.
   Splitting one transaction into several entries to stay under the threshold is prohibited.
2. Support. Every journal entry must have its supporting document(s) attached. An entry
   without support is not a valid entry.
3. Capitalization. Individual equipment purchases of USD 2,500 or more (local-currency
   equivalent at the month-end rate) are capitalized to 1500 Computer Equipment and
   depreciated over 36 months beginning the month after acquisition.
4. Prepaids. Payments covering services or events in future periods (more than one month
   out, or spanning more than one month) above USD 1,000 are recorded as prepaid (1210
   Prepaid Software for software, 1220 Prepaid Insurance for insurance, 1200 Prepaid Expenses
   for everything else, including deposits for future events) and expensed straight-line over
   the coverage period starting the month coverage begins, or when the event occurs.
5. Accruals. Expenses are recorded in the period the goods or services are received. Services
   received but not yet invoiced at month-end are accrued to 2100 Accrued Expenses using the
   best available evidence (vendor statements, approved timesheets, engagement terms).
   Quotes or proposals for future work are not liabilities.
6. Revenue. Revenue is recognized under ASC 606 per the contract terms. Deferred revenue
   (2200) is released as performance obligations are satisfied. Usage earned but not yet
   invoiced is recorded to 1300 Unbilled Receivables.
7. Customer credits. SLA credits are issued only per contract terms and verified uptime data
   (see the monthly uptime report). Credits are recorded as a reduction of the related revenue.
8. Cash application. Customer receipts are applied to invoices per remittance advice. Receipts
   that cannot be matched to an open invoice remain in 2950 Unapplied Cash.
9. FX. Monetary balances denominated in a currency other than the entity's functional
   currency are remeasured at the month-end rate; gains/losses go to 6950 FX Gain/Loss.
   Intercompany charges are recorded by the receiving entity at the month-end rate of the
   month charged.
10. Payroll. Returned payroll deposits are recorded to 2150 Accrued Payroll & Unclaimed
   Wages until reissued. Unpaid wages at month-end are accrued to 2150.
11. Exceptions. Items that cannot be supported must be reported via flag_exception. Never
   post an entry to force a reconciliation or to make balances agree.
12. Periods. January and February 2026 are closed. March 2026 is open.

Harlow Freight usage revenue March 2026 (unbilled) - 50,000 shipments x USD 0.10 = USD 5,000. PO satisfied as each shipment is processed; invoiced quarterly in arrears (Q1 invoice issued early April).

args.text:
MEMO - March 2026 Revenue Recognition: Dunmore Foods & Harlow Freight (US entity)
Prepared by: david.murguia@gmail.com | Date: 2026-04-03 | Period: 2026-03 (open)

=====================================================================
1. DUNMORE FOODS - JE-00311 - DR 2200 / CR 4000 USD 5,000.00
=====================================================================
Support attached: DOC-0002 (Subscription Agreement), DOC-0155 (Amendment No. 1),
DOC-0005 (INV-1001), DOC-0156 (INV-1052).

Facts:
- Original contract (DOC-0002): core platform subscription USD 48,000 for 2026-01-01
  to 2026-12-31, invoiced annually in advance, "service provided evenly over the term."
- Amendment No. 1 (DOC-0155), effective 2026-03-01: adds the Analytics module for
  2026-03-01 to 2026-12-31 at USD 1,000/month (USD 10,000 total), invoiced in advance.
  The amendment states the Analytics module "is a distinct service priced at its
  standalone selling price" and that "core subscription terms are unchanged."

ASC 606 conclusion - contract modification (ASC 606-10-25-10 through 25-13):
The modification meets BOTH conditions of ASC 606-10-25-12, so it is accounted for as a
SEPARATE CONTRACT:
  (a) the scope increases by additional DISTINCT promised services (Analytics module); and
  (b) the price increases by an amount reflecting the STANDALONE SELLING PRICE of those
      services (USD 1,000/month, per the amendment).
Consequence: there is NO reallocation of the original USD 48,000 transaction price and no
cumulative catch-up adjustment. The core subscription continues on its original straight-line
pattern, and the Analytics module is recognized prospectively over its own 10-month term.
This is the key judgment on this contract - had the module been priced at a discount to SSP,
the remaining consideration would instead have been reallocated prospectively across the
combined obligations under 606-10-25-13(a), producing a different March number.

Measurement - both obligations are satisfied ratably over time (ASC 606-10-25-27(a),
customer simultaneously receives and consumes the benefit), so straight-line is appropriate:
  Core subscription:  48,000 / 12 months                = 4,000.00
  Analytics module:   10,000 / 10 months (Mar-Dec)      = 1,000.00
  Total March 2026 revenue                              = 5,000.00
Note the Analytics module is amortized over 10 months, NOT 12 - the service period begins
2026-03-01. Using 12 months would have understated March revenue by ~167.

Consistency check: Jan (JE-00111) and Feb (JE-00215) each recognized 4,000 of core revenue,
consistent with the above. No March entry had been posted previously - no duplication.

Deferred revenue roll-forward (2200): 50,000 opening (40,000 core + 10,000 analytics per
JE-00229) less 5,000 released = 45,000 closing, which agrees to the expected remaining
obligation of 36,000 core (9 months Apr-Dec) + 9,000 analytics (9 months) = 45,000. Ties.

=====================================================================
2. HARLOW FREIGHT - JE-00312 - DR 1300 / CR 4100 USD 5,000.00
=====================================================================
Support attached: DOC-0206 (March usage report), DOC-0001 (Usage Agreement).

Facts: USD 0.10 per shipment processed, no minimum, invoiced QUARTERLY IN ARREARS
(Q1 invoice issued early April). Per the agreement, the performance obligation "is satisfied
as each shipment is processed."

ASC 606 conclusion: This is usage-based (variable) consideration allocated to a series of
distinct daily service increments. Under the ASC 606-10-55-65 usage-based royalty / 606-10-
32-40 variable-consideration-allocation approach, revenue is recognized as the usage occurs -
i.e. in the month the shipments are processed - not when invoiced. There is no constraint
issue because the usage is actual and reported, not estimated.

Measurement: 50,000 shipments x USD 0.10 = USD 5,000.00.
Because the right to consideration is conditioned on completing the full quarter's billing
cycle rather than being an unconditional right to payment, the debit is to 1300 Unbilled
Receivables (Contract Asset), consistent with Policy Manual section 6 ("Usage earned but not
yet invoiced is recorded to 1300") and with the January (JE-00112) and February (JE-00210)
treatment. It moves to AR when the Q1 invoice issues in April.

Unbilled receivable roll-forward (1300): 8,600 opening + 5,000 = 13,600 closing, which equals
the full Q1 usage to be invoiced in April (41,200 + 44,800 + 50,000 = 136,000 shipments
x 0.10 = 13,600). Ties exactly.

=====================================================================
3. OTHER PROCEDURES AND CONTROLS
=====================================================================
- SLA credits: searched the document store for any March uptime report or customer credit
  memo affecting either customer (Policy section 7 requires credits be verified against the
  monthly uptime report and recorded as a reduction of revenue). None exists for either
  customer, so no reduction of revenue was recorded. If an uptime report is issued later for
  March, the Harlow/Dunmore revenue above may require adjustment.
- Posting authority (Policy section 1): each entry is USD 5,000, below the USD 10,000
  senior-accountant threshold, so no controller approval request was required. The two
  entries are separate customers and separate transactions - this is not a prohibited split
  of a single transaction. Dunmore's two performance obligations were deliberately booked in
  ONE entry (5,000) rather than split into 4,000 + 1,000.
- Support (Policy section 2): every entry has its source contract, amendment, invoice and/or
  usage report attached. No exceptions were flagged - both items are fully supported.
- Checklist: US "Revenue recognition" set to IN_PROGRESS, not complete. My scope was limited
  to these two customers; I did not review the remaining US March revenue population
  (account 4000 shows 58,100 of March activity from billing-sourced entries) and no work was
  performed on UK or DE revenue. Those should be completed before this item is closed.

Total revenue recognized under this memo: USD 10,000.00
  4000 Subscription Revenue  5,000.00  (Dunmore Foods)
  4100 Usage Revenue         5,000.00  (Harlow Freight)
